item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Viva Insights: New Power BI report publishing capabilities for leaders
item.description:
[What and why]

We are expanding report publishing capabilities in Microsoft Viva Insights to include leaders, such as chief officers, managers, and their delegates. As part of this update, in Viva Feature Access Management, the Analyst report publish setting will be renamed to Report publish. This setting, which is on by default, will continue to be managed by Global Admins and Insights Admins, and will govern publishing for both analysts and leaders. This update enables leaders to directly publish and distribute curated Power BI reports available in Viva Insights without requiring an analyst to publish on their behalf.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide and GCC): Rollout begins in early November 2026 and is expected to complete by late November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Viva Insights report publishing capabilities.
  • Analysts, chief officers, managers, delegates, Insights Admins, and Global Admins.
  • Users who receive published Viva Insights reports.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Viva Insights
  • Power BI reports available through the Viva Insights Reports tab

What will happen

  • All analysts and leaders will be able to publish Power BI reports that are available to them in the Reports tab.
  • Users can publish either default or customized reports available to them.
  • Publishers can define the audience, report title, description, and publication end date.
  • Recipients will receive an email notification when a report is published to them, and can access published reports from the Viva Insights Reports tab.
  • Published reports can be shared using either: 
    • Unfiltered publish, where recipients view the report using the full data scope available for that report.
    • Manager-hierarchy publish, where recipients view the report based on the applicable manager hierarchy.
  • If a published report is configured to refresh weekly or monthly, the underlying query will continue to refresh until the publication end date.
  • Analysts and leaders will be able to manage published reports through the Manage publishes option.
  • Recipients can view and interact with published reports but cannot download reports, access row-level data, modify or manage publications, extend access, or republish reports.
  • If a publisher loses the qualifying role used to publish the report, recipients will retain access until the publication expires.
  • The existing Analyst report publish feature access control will be renamed to Report publish. This control will govern report publishing for analysts and leader personas, remains managed by Global Admins and Insights Admins, and is on by default.
  • Insights Admins will have visibility into published reports through the Admin Publish Reports experience, including the ability to view and remove publications and publish reports on behalf of users.

Setting up report properties prior to publishing

View and manage published reports

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you review your organization's report publishing governance and processes prior to rollout.

[Learn more]

  • Publish reports | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Backup: Activity Logs
item.description:
[What and why]

We're introducing activity logs in Microsoft 365 Backup to help administrators monitor backup policy and restore activities directly within the product. Activity logs provide greater visibility into configuration changes, restore progress, failures, and operational status without requiring administrators to leave the Microsoft 365 Backup experience.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Administrators who manage Microsoft 365 Backup

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Backup
  • SharePoint Online
  • OneDrive
  • Exchange Online

What will happen

  • Activity logs will be available for Microsoft 365 Backup actions across supported workloads, including SharePoint Online, OneDrive, and Exchange Online.
  • Activity log entries will include metadata such as service, activity type, status, impact, policy or restore task details, timestamps, and the administrator who performed the action.
  • Administrators will be able to:
    • Filter logs by service, activity type, activity status, impact, and date range.
    • Search activity logs using free text.
    • Export filtered or searched logs to CSV for offline review, reporting, and compliance workflows.
  • Role-based access controls will apply. Administrators will only be able to view logs for workloads they are authorized to manage.
  • To access this feature:

1. Go to the Microsoft 365 admin center.

2. Open Microsoft 365 Backup.

3. Select Recent activities to open the Activity logs page.

4. Use the date selector, search, or filters to review activity. Select Export to download the current result.

Activity logs in the Microsoft 365 admin center

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you inform your backup administrators that activity monitoring for Microsoft 365 Backup will be available directly within the product.

[Learn more]

We will update this post with new documentation.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft OneDrive: New pay-as-you-go storage billing option
item.description:
Updated October 6, 2026: We are no longer releasing to gov clouds at this time. We will communicate via a separate Message center post at a later date once we are ready to proceed with gov cloud release. If you are in a gov cloud, you can safely disregard this message. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We are introducing a pay-as-you-go, consumption-based billing option for additional OneDrive storage. This capability gives administrators more flexibility to manage storage growth by allowing selected OneDrive accounts to exceed their licensed storage quotas when needed, while helping organizations control which users can consume additional storage beyond their licensed storage quotas. Pay-as-you-go storage is currently in public preview for commercial tenants.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): The public preview of this feature is available now to all commercial tenants.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in early November 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft 365 commercial tenant administrators who manage OneDrive storage.
  • Organizations with OneDrive users approaching or exceeding their licensed storage quotas.

Platforms and services

  • OneDrive
  • Microsoft 365 admin and storage management experiences

What will happen

  • Administrators will be able to control which accounts are enabled to use a pay-as-you-go model to provide additional OneDrive storage beyond their licensed storage quotas.
  • Accounts enabled for storage consumption above their licensed storage quotas will be billed automatically based on usage.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required if you do not wish to use pay-as-you-go storage for your organization. We recommend that you:

  • Identify OneDrive accounts approaching or exceeding their licensed storage quotas.
  • Evaluate whether pay-as-you-go storage is appropriate for your organization.

[Learn more]

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Connected Platforms - Agent 365 extends observability to third-party agents
item.description:
Updated October 6, 2026: We have updated the timeline and content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Microsoft will roll out third-party agent observability in Microsoft Agent 365 to tenants. This lets you monitor the agents you sync from Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Anthropic Claude through Connected platforms in the same place as your Microsoft agents.

Administrators can see runs, sessions, tool calls, and exceptions on each agent’s Activity tab. The result: a more consistent way to understand agent usage and investigate issues across supported platforms without treating every environment as a separate monitoring exercise.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Public Preview (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on late October 2026 (previously late September) and expect to complete by late October 2026 (previously late September).

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out late November 2026 (previously late October) and expect to complete by late November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected

  • Administrators using Microsoft Agent 365 and Connected platforms
  • Organizations synchronizing agents from Amazon Bedrock Classic, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Google Vertex AI, or Anthropic Claude Managed Agents (preview)

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Agent 365
  • Connected platforms
  • Amazon Bedrock Classic
  • Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
  • Google Vertex AI
  • Anthropic Claude Managed Agents (preview)

What will happen

  • Agent 365 can collect observability data from supported third-party agent platforms.
  • Collected activity appears on each synchronized agent's Activity tab.
  • Runs, sessions, tool calls, and exceptions are mapped to the Agent 365 observability model.
  • Existing connections continue syncing agents as they do today.
  • Collection remains disabled for existing connections until an administrator enables it.
  • A new Collect agent observability data setting is available when creating or editing a supported connection.
  • The setting is enabled by default for new connections.
  • Agent 365 reads activity using existing connection credentials and does not execute agents.
  • Third-party providers may charge for tracing, storage, logging, or query services.
  • The Users metric is unavailable for synchronized third-party agents because Microsoft Entra identities are not provided by supported platforms.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • No action is required for existing connections.
  • Enable Collect agent observability data on existing connections if observability is desired.
  • Validate source platform permissions and telemetry configuration.
  • Clear the Collect agent observability data option during setup if collection is not desired for a new connection.

Platform Requirements

  • Amazon Bedrock Classic: Enable trace capture to Amazon S3 and grant read access to the activity bucket.
  • Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Enable CloudWatch Transaction Search and grant access to query CloudWatch log groups.
  • Google Vertex AI: Assign required BigQuery, Monitoring, and Cloud Trace roles; enable APIs; enable telemetry collection and Trace Analytics BigQuery export.
  • Anthropic Claude Managed Agents (preview): No additional setup required.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. The feature uses AI/ML or agent capabilities with Microsoft 365 content, prompts, or service data as described in this message.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify any capability that enables users to automate workflows through AI or bot agents?Yes. The feature introduces or updates agent-related AI capabilities as described in this message.
Does the change include an admin control and, can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. The feature includes or affects admin controls, policies, permissions, roles, authentication, or management settings as described in this message. Review the linked documentation or admin center controls for group-based configuration support.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Improved file sharing experience in external chats
item.description:
Updated October 6, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We’re improving the file-sharing experience in Microsoft Teams external (federated) chats by making the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences available by default. This change only impacts tenants who have not adjusted the policy that controls file attachment in an external Teams chat. To opt out of this change, disable the capability using the Teams PowerShell setting provided in the “Action required and recommendations” section below. This can be done before the rollout and your policy setting will be respected. This update does not change your OneDrive or SharePoint external-sharing settings or override existing access restrictions. 

Prior to this change, when existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies allow, users can already share files in external chats by sharing a link to the file. This update makes that flow easier by adding the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences directly in Teams. Files uploaded from the user’s device are stored in the sender’s OneDrive, while cloud files remain stored in their existing location. Teams then assigns permissions to chat participants, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing policies. Senders can still review, modify, or remove file access before sending the message. This reduces the need to assign permissions manually, while allowing senders to stay in control.

  • More info: Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams external access (federation)
  • This change applies only to organizations where the setting has not been explicitly configured. Any customers who have left the configuration in the default state will be impacted. 
  • Users participating in external 1:1 chats, external group chats, and meeting chats

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • External (federated) 1:1 chats
  • External (federated) group chats
  • Meeting chats
  • Teams desktop app
  • Teams web app

What will happen

  • The ability for users to attach and share files in external chats will be enabled for all Microsoft 365 tenants, unless your organization has previously explicitly disabled this setting in Teams. Any customers who have left the configuration in the default state will be impacted.
  • Users can already paste file links into external chants. This ability is unchanged. With this change, users will also have the ability to attach and share files using the paperclip option or drag and drop in external (federated) chats.
  • Files shared through these experiences continue to be stored and shared through OneDrive or SharePoint. Files uploaded from a user’s device are stored in the sender’s OneDrive, while existing cloud files remain in their current location. 
  • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns permissions to participants in the external chat for files uploaded using paperclip or drag-and-drop, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies.
  • Senders can review, modify, or remove sharing permissions before sending a file.
  • Senders can continue to modify or revoke access after a file has been shared.
  • Automatic permission assignment applies only to files shared through the paperclip or drag-and-drop experience.
  • The files will be shared as hyperlinks after send. 
  • Existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing controls continue to govern access.
  • Existing sensitivity labels, domain restrictions, and security protections continue to apply.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required to preserve external-sharing restrictions already configured in OneDrive and SharePoint; this update does not change those restrictions. To review or change these controls, see Manage sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive in Microsoft 365. 

[To disable file attachments in external chats]

To opt out of this change, apply the following Teams PowerShell setting if you have not already explicitly configured this setting:

Set-CsTeamsFilesPolicy -Identity Global -FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers Disabled

Verify the setting:

Get-CsTeamsFilesPolicy | Select Identity, FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers

Recommended actions:

  • Review your SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Entra external sharing configuration because these settings continue to govern what external recipients can access.
  • Inform helpdesk and support teams about the updated attachment experience and the distinction between Teams attachment controls and OneDrive/SharePoint access controls. 
  • Update user training and internal documentation as needed.
  • Communicate to users that:
    • They can attach files directly in chats with people outside the organization.
    • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns chat participants access to files shared via paperclip icon, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies. Senders can review, modify, or remove access before sending.
    • Pasted file links retain their existing permissions.
    • Files uploaded to external chats are stored in the sender's OneDrive and display.

Optional configuration to allow attachments without automatic permission assignment:

To disable automatic permission assignment while continuing to allow file attachments in external chats:

Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity Global -AutoShareFilesInExternalChats Disabled

If automatic permission assignment is disabled, users may need to manually grant access to shared files before external recipients can open them.

Allow several hours for policy changes to propagate before users see the updated experience.

Learn more:

  • Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Uploaded files shared through Attach or drag-and-drop can automatically receive permissions for participants in external chats. Existing OneDrive and SharePoint controls continue to govern access. Uploaded files are stored in the sender’s OneDrive.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?Yes. The direct file-attachment experience in external (federated) chats becomes available by default; the existing ability to paste file links remains unchanged.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins can separately control Teams file attachments and automatic permission assignment through Teams PowerShell policies. OneDrive and SharePoint sharing settings continue to govern external file access.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) [Outlook Mac] Purview Data Loss Prevention support for Calendar Events
item.description:
Updated October 6, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why:]

Outlook for Mac will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention \(DLP\) policies for calendar events. Organizations can detect and help prevent the sharing of sensitive information in meeting subjects, descriptions, and invite content through policy tips, user remediation, and policy enforcement. This provides consistent compliance protection across email and calendar experiences on Mac devices.

[Rollout schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out mid-November 2026 (previously late September) and expect to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late September).

[Impact on your organization:]

This feature helps organizations extend Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention protections to calendar events created in Outlook for Mac. Users receive policy guidance before sending meeting invitations that contain sensitive information, helping reduce accidental data exposure and improve compliance. Organizations benefit from more consistent protection across email and calendar workflows while supporting regulatory and corporate data protection requirements.

[Action required, Recommendations:]

No administrator action is required to prepare for this feature. Existing Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention policies will automatically apply to supported calendar events in Outlook for Mac. Organizations with DLP policies already configured can benefit from expanded protection of calendar content without additional policy creation or client configuration. Administrators may choose to review existing DLP policies to ensure they align with their organization's compliance requirements.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) [Outlook Mac] Purview DLP Wait-on-Send Support

Outlook for Mac will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention \(DLP\) wait\-on\-send policies. Organizations can require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent and configure how long users must wait for policy evaluation to complete. This helps ensure sensitive information is inspected against organizational policies before messages leave the organization while providing administrators with flexible control over the user experience.

[Rollout schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out mid-November 2026 (previously late September) and expect to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late September).

[Impact on your organization:]

This feature helps organizations reduce the risk of sensitive information being sent before Microsoft Purview DLP policies can be evaluated. Administrators can require users to wait for policy inspection and configure the maximum wait time based on organizational requirements. This improves policy enforcement and compliance while allowing organizations to balance security, performance, and user productivity.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

Administrators can review their existing Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention policies and determine whether wait-on-send enforcement is appropriate for their organization. To take advantage of this feature, administrators may enable and configure the desired wait period within supported DLP policies. No changes are required for organizations that do not plan to use wait-on-send enforcement.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Outlook for Mac: Sensitivity label recommendations and auto-labeling from attachments
item.description:
Updated October 6, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

We're introducing support in Outlook for Mac that can automatically apply or recommend Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels based on the sensitivity labels assigned to attached files.

This enhancement helps organizations apply more consistent information protection by aligning email sensitivity labels with the classification of attached content. By reducing the need for manual labeling, organizations can help lower the risk of misclassified communications and support compliance and data protection objectives.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 (previously late September) and is expected to complete in mid-November 2026 (previously late September).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who compose email messages in Outlook for Mac.
  • Organizations that use Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels.

Platforms and Services:

  • Outlook for Mac
  • Microsoft Purview Information Protection

What will happen:

  • When users attach files that already have Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels, Outlook for Mac can automatically apply or recommend an appropriate sensitivity label for the email message.
  • Email classification can better align with the sensitivity of attached content.
  • Depending on your organization's label policies, users may see sensitivity label recommendations or automatic label application while composing messages.
  • This capability helps reduce manual labeling effort and promotes a more consistent information protection experience across Outlook clients.

[Action Required / Recommendations:]

No admin action is required.

We recommend that organizations using Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels:

  • Review existing sensitivity label publishing and protection policies.
  • Validate that attachment-based label inheritance behavior aligns with organizational compliance and information protection requirements.
  • Inform compliance, security, and support teams of the upcoming change so they can address user questions.

[Compliance Considerations:]

IssueExplanation
Microsoft Purview labeling behaviorThis change affects how Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels may be applied or recommended for email messages based on the sensitivity labels of attached files.
Information protection and compliance workflowsOrganizations should verify that automatic or recommended label inheritance aligns with their existing classification and protection requirements.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Legal agent available in Frontier worldwide
item.description:
Updated October 6, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.  

[What and Why]

Microsoft is expanding the availability of the Legal agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word to Frontier users worldwide in Public Preview.

The Legal agent was previously released in Frontier preview for users located in the United States only. This update expands access globally, enabling more organizations to benefit from this capability.

The Legal agent is a vertical-specific Microsoft 365 Copilot experience designed for legal professionals, built directly into Word. It helps legal teams review and negotiate contracts by identifying risks, comparing clauses to internal playbooks, and proposing edits using Word’s native tracked changes.

This update helps reduce manual review time while keeping legal professionals fully in control of document workflows.

[Rollout Schedule]

  • Frontier Preview: Available starting in mid-June 2026.
  • General Availability: Available starting mid-October 2026 (previously early October).

[Impact on Your Organization] 

Who is affected

  • Organizations enrolled in the Microsoft 365 Copilot Frontier program
  • Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, particularly legal professionals (for example, in-house counsel, contract managers, legal ops)

Organizations not enrolled in the Frontier program are not impacted.

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Word (Copilot) – desktop
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot (Frontier)

What will happen

  • A new Legal agent will be available in Copilot Chat in Word via the “+” (plus) menu.
  • Users can:
    • Review contracts to identify risks and non-standard clauses
    • Generate redlines using Word tracked changes
    • Compare clauses against internal legal playbooks
    • Analyze document sections for compliance with internal standards
    • Receive responses grounded in document content with citations
  • The feature is enabled by default for tenants enrolled in Frontier.
  • No separate installation is required.
  • The feature is available immediately after users update to a supported version of Word.
  • Availability depends on:
    • Frontier program enrollment
    • Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing
  • There is no dedicated admin or user toggle to disable this feature
  • Access is controlled through Frontier enrollment and Copilot license assignment.

[Action Required / Recommendations]

No action is required if you do not plan to use this feature.

If you plan to use this feature:

  • Enroll your tenant in the Frontier Public Preview program.
  • Ensure Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses are assigned to eligible users.
  • Review internal legal workflows that may benefit from:
    • Contract analysis
    • Playbook-based reviews
    • AI-assisted redlining
  • Communicate this capability to legal teams.
  • Update internal documentation or helpdesk guidance if applicable.

[Compliance considerations]

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint: Generate smart tables of contents for PDFs on the web with Copilot
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We are introducing Smart Table of Contents (Smart TOC) in the Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint PDF viewer on the web for users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. When a PDF does not already contain a table of contents, users can ask Copilot to generate a hierarchical, clickable structure that makes it easier to navigate long documents and move between sections. This feature is available only on the web in the initial release and is generated only when a user explicitly requests it.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.
  • General Availability (GCC): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.
  • General Availability (GCC High): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.
  • General Availability (DoD): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.

This is a gradual rollout, and not all eligible users will receive the feature at the same time.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

  • Who is affected: Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license who access PDF files in OneDrive and SharePoint on the web.
  • Platforms/Services: OneDrive, SharePoint, Microsoft 365 Copilot, PDF viewer on the web.

What will happen:

  • The Smart TOC entry point will appear when an eligible user opens a PDF that does not already contain table-of-contents information.
  • The feature is available only in the OneDrive and SharePoint PDF viewer on the web during the initial release.
  • Mobile and desktop applications are not included at this time.
  • Copilot analyzes document structure and generates nested, clickable entries mapped to pages or page ranges.
  • Users with edit permissions can save the generated table of contents into the PDF.
  • The saved table of contents can be displayed by compatible PDF editors.
  • Users with view-only permissions can generate and use Smart TOC for navigation but cannot save the generated table of contents.
  • Smart TOC is available only to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • AI-generated content may be inaccurate, particularly for scanned or OCR-based PDF files.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No immediate admin action is required.

Before rollout, you may want to:

  • Review Microsoft 365 Copilot license assignments for users who should have access to this capability.
  • Inform eligible users, helpdesk personnel, and support teams about the new PDF navigation experience.
  • Update internal documentation to clarify that saving a generated table of contents requires edit permissions on the PDF.
  • Encourage users to validate AI-generated table-of-contents entries when accuracy is important.

[Compliance considerations:]

  • Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed? Yes. Copilot processes PDF content that the licensed user is already authorized to access in order to generate a table of contents for navigation. Existing file permissions are respected, and saving changes requires edit permissions.
  • Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data? Yes. Copilot analyzes PDF document structure and generates an AI-created hierarchical table of contents. The experience is user-initiated and does not run automatically.
  • Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI? Yes. Eligible users can request Copilot to generate a table of contents for PDF files that do not already contain one.
  • Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves? Yes. The feature is user-initiated and only runs when a licensed user chooses to generate a Smart TOC.

The experience will clearly indicate that the table of contents was AI generated and may contain inaccuracies.

item.description:

[What and why]

We are improving the OneDrive sync experience on Windows desktop to provide clearer, more actionable guidance when file and folder paths exceed the supported 520-character limit. The updated experience will show exactly how many characters a path exceeds the limit and will provide a guided flow to rename or move affected items so they can sync successfully.

This improvement addresses a common OneDrive sync issue by reducing user confusion, minimizing workflow disruption, and helping users resolve errors faster.

This update is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 557563.

[Rollout schedule]

General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning end of October 2026 (previously early October) and expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously end of October)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • All users of the OneDrive sync client on Windows desktop

Platforms and services

  • OneDrive for Business (Windows desktop sync client)

What will happen

Max path errors are one of the most commonly reported issues by OneDrive sync users. Currently, when a file or folder path exceeds the 520-character sync limit, the error message only states how many characters the path exceeds the limit and asks users to shorten it. In addition, File Explorer limitations may prevent users from renaming paths over 260 characters, and the sync client may stop syncing until the issue is resolved.

As part of this improved error experience, when users encounter max path errors, the sync client will continue running and users will be guided through a custom rename and move experience.

With this update:

  • The sync client will continue running when users encounter max path errors
  • Users will be guided through a custom rename and move experience to resolve issues directly

The rename experience will:

  • Show the number of over-limit characters
  • Highlight which items in the path can be renamed
  • Allow renames even when the path exceeds 260 characters

Screenshot - Custom rename dialog

The move experience will:

  • Show over-limit character counts in a guided interface
  • Display warning dialogs for over-limit shared items in OneDrive
  • Display warning dialogs for over-limit items in shortcuts

Screenshot - Example warning dialog for overlimit items in shortcuts

These enhancements are designed to reduce troubleshooting time and improve the overall sync experience.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required. This update will be automatically available through the OneDrive sync client.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Migrate Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing before EWS deprecation
item.description:
Updated October 5, 2026: Gov rollout of this feature is paused at this time. We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for any inconvenience.

[What and Why:]

Exchange Web Services (EWS) deprecation begins October 1, 2026. Cross-tenant collaboration features — Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing — currently rely on EWS.

Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips will be available by September 2026 and Calendar Sharing will be available by mid-October 2026 via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy, which replaces EWS-based cross-tenant collaboration.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in August 2026 and expect to complete by September 15, 2026 for Free/Busy, Mailtips and October 15, 2026 for Calendar Sharing.
  • GCC, GCC High, DoD: We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[Impact on your organization:]

Sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips (e.g., out of office message) with another Microsoft 365 organization via Organization Relationship or Sharing Policy relies on Exchange Web Services (EWS), which is being deprecated. To preserve these cross-tenant collaboration scenarios, you will need to start migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policy.

Your tenant is affected if it uses any of the following Exchange Online configurations:

  • Organization Relationships — sharing Free/Busy or MailTips with other Microsoft 365 tenants 
  • Sharing Policies — sharing calendars externally, either via invitations sent to recipients in other Microsoft 365 organizations or calendars published for anonymous access via an internet URL

Run these commands in Exchange Online PowerShell to check if your tenant is affected: 

    • Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScopeIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) either FreeBusyAccessEnabled: True or MailtipsAccessEnabled: True, and (3) the external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed. 
    • Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Domains, Enabled, DefaultIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) the Domains property contains at least one rule with a CalendarSharingFreeBusy access level (Simple, Detail, or Reviewer), and (3) the targeted external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, and (4) the policy is assigned to one or more mailboxes, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed.
    • Note: rules that begin with Anonymous: represent calendar publishing to anonymous internet recipients via a published URL - these also appear in this output.

What happens if I do nothing:

Starting October 1, 2026, Exchange Web Services (EWS) will be gradually disabled in line with previous communications linked to this message. As this rollout reaches your tenant, cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing that rely on EWS will be affected — recipients in partner organizations may no longer see Free/Busy, MailTips, or shared calendars from your tenant. 

If your organization is not ready to migrate, you can retain EWS access by following the guidance of the latest blog we published: ExchangeOnline EWS, Your Time is Almost Up (EWSEnabled set to True) while you prepare and execute the migration steps attached to this message. EWS access through this extension will remain available until the final EWS shutdown on April 1, 2027. 

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Follow this Message center post for updates to the rollout schedule. To avoid impact, plan to migrate after the rollout reaches your tenant and before EWS deprecation.
  • Review the migration guide linked below for step-by-step instructions to understand your current configurations, set up new Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policies, validate the new configurations, and remove unused configurations. 
  • Check the blog post linked below for additional information and answers to frequently asked questions. 
  • Hybrid and on-premises scenarios are not in scope. This update applies to fully cloud-hosted (Exchange Online ↔ Exchange Online) cross-tenant and cross-cloud configurations only. For organizations running on-premises Exchange and Exchange Online in a Hybrid Deployment, migrate to Dedicated Hybrid App. For organizations hosted in Exchange Online sharing with another organization running Exchange on-premises, kindly monitor future Message Center posts for guidance on migration paths as they become available.

item.title: [planForChange] Dynamics 365 and Power Platform– Information about storage validation for Dataverse-only tenants
item.description:
Beginning November 9, 2026, we are introducing staged storage validation for supported Dynamics 365 applications. The change gives administrators clearer visibility into storage use, advance notice of potential restrictions, and several ways to remain within capacity, including removing unneeded data, adding capacity, or enabling pay-as-you-go for sandbox environments.

When a tenant exceeds its entitled Database, File, or Log capacity, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations will be restricted immediately. If the overage remains unresolved, sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go billing enabled will enter Administration mode after 30 days of remaining over capacity, allowing access only to administrators. After 60 days, those sandbox environments will be disabled, preventing access for all users. Production environments are not subject to these restrictions and will remain accessible. However, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations will still be blocked while the tenant remains over capacity.

Deployment Timeline:
  • Rollout begins: November 9, 2026
  • Rollout completion: December 4, 2026
How does this affect me?
The Dataverse storage validation applies only to Dataverse-only tenants without Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations environment(s) or consumption. The products in-scope of storage validation include:
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Field Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Voice
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact Center
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Project Operations (Dataverse deployments)
If your tenant exceeds its entitled storage capacity, the following lifecycle applies:

Stage Timing Impact
1. Restricted When the tenant first exceeds its entitled storage capacity, known as time zero (T0) Environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations are blocked
2. Administration mode 30 days after the tenant first exceeds capacity - T0 Only administrators can sign in to *affected sandbox environments. All other users are blocked from accessing the environment.
3. Disabled After 60 unresolved days from T0 All users, including administrators, are blocked from *affected sandbox environments; the environment data is retained and remains available for recovery after remediation

Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing do not progress through the storage overage lifecycle. Other *affected sandbox environments in the tenant may still be affected with restrictions.

We will provide notifications that include the tenant's current storage status, the date it first exceeded capacity, its current lifecycle stage, upcoming restrictions, and recommended remediation actions.

Restrictions are removed after the tenant has returned below 100% of its entitled storage capacity. Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing are excluded from the lifecycle even if the tenant remains over storage capacity. Processing time may vary depending on the remediation method used.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Teams admin center device state rules and health alerts retire; use Teams Rooms Pro Management portal

As part of the ongoing transition of Teams device management from the Microsoft Teams admin center (TAC) to the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal (PMP), we are retiring device health monitoring capabilities in TAC — specifically the Device state rule (Teams admin center > Notifications & alerts > Rules) and the device health alerts it generates.

Going forward, device health monitoring for all Teams devices (MTR-A, Phones, Panels etc.) is delivered through the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal, which provides device health signals, monitoring, and incident management in a single unified portal. This is a continuation of the change previously communicated in MC1227622, where Android device management capabilities including inventory, updates, health monitoring, and settings transitioned from TAC to PMP.

What will happen:

  1. The Device state rule page under Notifications & alerts > Rules in the Teams admin center will no longer be available, and existing rule configurations will stop being evaluated.
  2. Device offline / health alerts will stop being delivered to the Admin Alerts and Notifications team's MonitoringAlerts channel.

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center - Use role-based enforcement for recording and transcription downloads
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to use role-based enforcement for recording and transcription downloads in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. This feature will reach general availability on October 31, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature helps organizations better protect sensitive customer communications by separating permissions to view recordings and transcripts from permissions to download them. Admins can assign new Dataverse security roles to prevent selected users from downloading recordings or transcripts while still allowing them to view and play back content as permitted by existing access.

The two new Dataverse security roles that will be available are:
  • Deny Recording Download
  • Deny Transcription Download
When either role is assigned to a user:
  • The user can continue to view and play back recordings and transcripts as permitted by existing access.
  • The user is blocked from downloading the corresponding artifact.
Enforcement of these models is applied server-side across the Dynamics 365 Contact Center UI, public and internal APIs, and direct download URLs or integrations. Download requests will also be denied regardless of how they are initiated.

Access control is driven entirely by Dataverse role assignment. The deny roles override implicit download behavior without affecting recording, transcription, or playback functionality.

These controls help reduce the risk of unauthorized data export, support compliance and data governance requirements, and allow organizations to maintain operational visibility without allowing data removal.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Exchange Online: Exchange Web Services (EWS) enforcement update for EWSAllowedAppIDs
item.description:
[What and why]

As previously communicated in MC1466860 and MC1447678, Microsoft is continuing the retirement of Exchange Web Services (EWS) in Exchange Online.

Beginning October 10, 2026, setting EWSEnabled=True will no longer be sufficient to allow EWS access for affected Worldwide tenants. Organizations that require EWS must configure EWSAllowedAppIDs to specify which applications are permitted to access EWS.

This change is part of the final phase of EWS retirement and is intended to help organizations identify EWS dependencies, reduce service disruption, and support migration planning.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD: Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete by early July 2027

Key milestones for Worldwide tenants with EWSEnabled=True and no configured EWSAllowedAppIDs list:

DateMilestone
October 2, 2026Microsoft identifies affected Worldwide tenants. After this date, tenants that enable EWS must configure EWSAllowedAppIDs themselves.
October 8-9, 2026Microsoft creates and populates EWSAllowedAppIDs for qualifying Worldwide tenants based on EWS activity observed during the previous 60 days.
October 10, 2026EWSAllowedAPPIDs becomes required when EWSEnabled=True. Applications note included in the allow list may lose access to EWS.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Exchange Online administrators
  • Organizations that continue to use applications or services that depend on EWS
  • Tenants with EWSEnabled=True

Platforms and services

  • Exchange Online
  • Exchange Web Services (EWS)

What will happen

  • Beginning October 10, 2026, affected Worldwide tenants with EWSEnabled=True must have a configured EWSAllowedAppIDs allow list. Applications not included in the allow list may lose access to EWS.
  • For identified Worldwide tenants with EWSEnabled=True and no configured EWSAllowedAppIDs list on October 3 2026, Microsoft creates and populates an allow list using EWS activity observed during the previous 60 days. Infrequently used applications may not be identified.
  • Cross-tenant organization relationships are not affected by the EWSAllowedAppIDs requirement.
  • Organizations remain responsible for reviewing, validating, and maintaining EWSAllowedAppIDs.
  • EWSAllowedAppIDs is a replacement list. Ensure all required AppIDs are included whenever the configuration is updated.
  • Microsoft applications and scenarios that may generate EWS traffic include Outlook for Windows, Classic Outlook for Mac, Excel Power Query, Power BI, and Exchange Server hybrid scenarios.
  • Outlook for Windows customers should be on August 2026 build 16.0.20430.20092 or later. If EWS-related issues continue after disabling EWS, the cause may be customer-forced configuration. Test whether blocking EWS for the Office client AppID is possible without impact.
  • New Outlook for Mac is not affected. If your organization continues to use Classic Outlook for Mac, ensure the Microsoft Office AppID is included in EWSAllowedAppIDs.
  • Tenants with EWSEnabled not configured (Null) remain subject to Microsoft's phased EWS retirement process and will have EWS disabled as part of that rollout.
  • Organizations with EWSEnabled=True and a configured EWSAllowedAppIDs allow list will not have their EWSEnabled setting modified by Microsoft before April 2027.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization relies on EWS:

  • Review EWS usage reports and identify applications and services that require continued EWS access.
  • Configure and validate an EWSAllowedAppIDs allow list before October 10, 2026.
  • Include Microsoft first-party applications that continue to rely on EWS if they appear in your usage reporting.
  • Ensure all required AppIDs are included whenever EWSAllowedAppIDs is updated.
  • Keep the allow list current as applications are added, removed, or migrated away from EWS.
  • Enable EWS only when required for approved applications.
  • Continue planning migration from EWS to Microsoft Graph where possible.

To verify the configured allow list: Get-OrganizationConfig -RetrieveEwsOperationAccessPolicy | Format-List EwsAllowedAppIDs

Allow up to 24 hours for EWSAllowedAppIDs changes to take effect and approximately one hour for EWSEnabled changes.

Important: EWSAllowList is unrelated to EWS retirement and does not replace EWSAllowedAppIDs.

Learn more

  • Exchange Online EWS, Your Time is Almost Up | Microsoft Community Hub
  • How to revert the Outlook Desktop WebView based Room Finder to the legacy Room Finder | Microsoft Support
  • Impact of Exchange Online EWS Deprecation on Hybrid Rich Coexistence and Cross-org Sharing | Microsoft Community Hub
  • Notes from the field: testing EWSAllowedAppIDs safely | Microsoft Community Hub

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change include an admin control?Yes. EWSAllowedAppIDs introduces a tenant-level administrative control that allows Exchange Online administrators to explicitly define which applications are permitted to access EWS.
Does this change alter how existing customer data is accessed?Yes. The change modifies how applications are authorized to access Exchange Online data through EWS by requiring administrators to explicitly allow approved application IDs as retirement enforcement begins.
Does this change alter how admins monitor, manage, or demonstrate compliance-related activities?Yes. Administrators must identify EWS dependencies, configure and maintain an EWSAllowedAppIDs allow list, and validate application access as part of preparing for EWS retirement.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Retirement of SharePoint One-Time Passcode (SPO OTP) and transition to Microsoft Entra B2B
item.description:
Updated October 1, 2026: Phase 1, which enables Entra B2B for new external sharing, is now fully rolled out for Production environments. To ensure a smooth transition, Phase 2, the retirement of SharePoint Online OTP, has been rescheduled to begin in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by end of November 2026 for Production environments.

Both Phase 1 and Phase 2 roll outs exclude GCC, GCCH & DoD. New dates for these environments will be communicated via Message center when we are ready to proceed. Thank you for your patience.

[Introduction]

We are retiring SharePoint One‑Time Passcode (SPO OTP) authentication in OneDrive and SharePoint starting mid-October 2026. Beginning in May 2026, new external sharing invitations and authentication will start using Microsoft Entra B2B instead of SPO OTP. This transition simplifies external collaboration, aligns authentication with Microsoft identity standards, and enables consistent guest lifecycle management, governance, and Conditional Access coverage across Microsoft 365.

[When this will happen]

  • May & June 2026: Invitation and authentication for new external sharing transitions to Microsoft Entra B2B. Users who previously authenticated via SPO OTP will continue to have access to specific people links even without a B2B guest account yet.
  • Mid-October 2026: Retirement of SPO OTP authentication begins. External users without a guest account get access denied on previously shared specific people links. To restore access, a guest account must be created in Entra B2B, or an allowed user must share/re-share at least one file/folder/site.
  • Retirement is expected to complete by end of November 2026.

[How this affects your organization]

Who is affected

  • All Microsoft 365 tenants (commercial, government, sovereign).
  • All external users who access OneDrive or SharePoint files, folders, or sites.

What will happen

  • The EnableAzureADB2BIntegration setting will no longer control external sharing behavior beginning May 2026.
  • SPO OTP authentication will retire beginning mid-October 2026.
  • The option to disable Entra B2B integration will be removed.

Impact on external users

  • External users who already have an Entra B2B guest account in your directory:
    • No change in behavior.
  • External users without a B2B guest account:
    • Specific people links shared after changes rolled out to your tenant: A guest account will be automatically created via the Entra B2B Invitation Manager and authentication will use Entra B2B. The email one-time passcode feature is now turned on by default for all new tenants and for any existing tenants where you haven’t explicitly turned it off. Please refer to this article to learn more.
    • Specific people links shared before changes rolled out to your tenant: SPO OTP authentication continues until the retirement reaches the tenant. After the retirement, these users will receive access denied until a matching B2B guest account exists.

Restoring access after retirement

  • Admins can manually create a guest account for the external user at any time. Alternatively, an internal user with permissions needs to share or re-share at least one file, folder, or site, which will automatically create the guest account and restore access to all previously shared content.

[What you need to do to prepare]

To ensure a smooth transition:

  • Review external sharing policies and conditional access settings for guests in SharePoint and Entra admin centers.
  • Ensure that Microsoft Entra is configured to allow guest invitations for the appropriate users. For example, assign the Guest Inviter role to users who need external sharing or are responsible for creating guest accounts.
  • Inform users that, beginning in mid-October 2026, some external collaborators may see an access denied message when opening older links that were previously authenticated with SharePoint Online OTP. This can occur if a matching B2B guest account was not created for the email address used with the original sharing link.
    • To restore access, users can share or reshare at least one file with the external collaborator. This creates the required B2B guest account, after which the collaborator can continue accessing previously shared links.
  • If your organization relies on email OTP authentication via Entra, ensure it is not disabled in Entra External ID settings. See Email OTP for B2B guests.
  • Optionally, identify external collaborators without guest accounts via external sharing reports. Proactively create guest accounts to retain access.
  • Update internal documentation.

Learn more:

  • Add and manage B2B collaboration users in the Microsoft Entra admin center | External ID | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Learn
  • Email one-time passcode authentication for B2B guest users | External ID | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Learn
  • Frequently Asked Questions: Improvements to external sharing in OneDrive & SharePoint | SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
  • Overview: B2B collaboration with external guests for your workforce | External ID | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Learn
  • Quickstart: Add a guest user and send an invitation | External ID | Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Learn
  • SharePoint and OneDrive integration with Microsoft Entra B2B | SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
  • Configure external collaboration - Microsoft Entra External ID | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

Compliance QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is accessed, processed, or stored?Yes. This change retires SPO OTP authentication and requires all external users to authenticate using Microsoft Entra B2B guest accounts, which alters the authentication method used to access existing SharePoint and OneDrive content.
Does the change modify Conditional Access policies or enforcement?Yes. After retirement, all external users will authenticate through Entra B2B and become fully subject to Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, Identity Protection, and guest governance policies.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?Yes. External sharing invitations will be routed through Microsoft Entra B2B Invitation Manager instead of SharePoint’s OTP invitation flow.
Does the change alter how admins monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Authentication events and guest lifecycle actions will be logged through Entra audit logs rather than SPO OTP logs, changing where admins review authentication and guest access activity.

[What and why:]

We're introducing the third-generation Microsoft 365 sharing experience to make collaboration simpler, smarter, and more secure by default. At the center of this update is a new hero link—a single sharing link that controls access to a file or folder.

Users will see one consistent sharing experience whether they copy a link, share through email, or use the browser URL. The hero link consolidates sharing controls into a single link that can be updated after it has been shared, reducing the need to create and resend new links when access requirements change.

[Rollout schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rolling out early October 2026 (previously mid-September) through late October 2026

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected: All users who share or manage files and folders in Microsoft 365.

Platforms and services: SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 file-sharing experiences.

What will happen:

  • Every file and folder will have a single primary sharing link, called the hero link, displayed in the sharing dialog.
  • The hero link settings determine who can access the item beyond people who are explicitly granted access.
  • Adding people directly to a file or folder remains unchanged and continues to be the simplest way to share content.

Screenshot - Add people screen when sharing 

  • By default, the hero link is set to Only people added to the file, meaning the link itself does not grant access to anyone.

Screenshot - Share file view with hero link

  • Users can broaden access to people in the organization with the link or, where permitted by organizational policy, to anyone with the link.
  • Users can choose whether recipients can view, edit, or view without downloading, depending on available permissions.
  • Changing the audience for the hero link updates the existing link rather than creating a new one.
  • If recipients cannot open a previously shared file, the sender can expand access on the same hero link without redistributing a new URL.
  • Existing sharing links will continue to function and will appear under Other links in the sharing dialog.
  • Effective access remains the most permissive combination of direct permissions, inherited permissions, group-based permissions, and link-based permissions.
  • Users will see a tutorial experience upon opening the new share dialog for the first time.

[Action required/Recommendations:]

No action is required before rollout.

Organizations should consider the following preparation activities:

  • Review internal sharing guidance and end-user documentation to reflect the new single-link sharing model.
  • Communicate the updated sharing experience to users who regularly collaborate across teams and organizations.
  • Evaluate site-level default sharing settings where different sharing behaviors are required.

Admin controls

  • Administrators can configure the default audience for the hero link at the SharePoint site collection or OneDrive level by using the DefaultMainLinkScope parameter in SharePoint PowerShell.
  • Supported values are:
    • OnlyPeopleAdded (default)
    • Organization
  • There is currently no tenant-wide equivalent setting for the hero link audience.
  • DefaultMainLinkScope controls only the default audience and does not prevent users from broadening access when allowed by policy.
  • Hero links start with view permissions by default.
  • Existing default sharing link settings and link expiration policies continue to apply to legacy links and do not govern hero links.
